title: arXiv imposes submission limits amid surge in AI-generated papers
key_facts: arXiv received a record 40,363 submissions in September 2026, against 20,569 in September 2024 and 9,869 in September 2016.
The surge produced almost 9,000 support tickets for staff and moderators.
From 1 October 2026 each author may make two submissions per calendar month and have no more than three active submissions at once.
arXiv calls the limits a stopgap while it decides best practice for authors using advanced AI tools and improves moderation.
Submissions to the cs.AI category rose more than sixfold in two years; other categories roughly doubled.
Moderators report more 'thin' papers, 'salami' papers (one study split into several) and dense AI-written papers.
arXiv still permits AI tools if use is disclosed and papers meet its standards.
quote_evidence: As of October 1st, 2026, arXiv is instituting an updated rate limiting policy across all submitters and categories as a stopgap...
a relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time.
The organisation said the new limits are an interim measure...
why_it_matters_hint: Volunteer moderators were overloaded and honest authors' papers were delayed by days or weeks.
notes: Policy took effect 1 Oct 2026, before the 6 Oct cutoff, so freshness is a follow-up and the score is lowered by one. Related to the 6 Oct item 'arXiv might not survive AI slop onslaught' but not the same story.
